note.text: An idea or concept is what we grasp mentally; a term is its expression in language. A term can contain several words, such as school library. In traditional terminology, intension or comprehension concerns the defining attributes of a concept, while extension concerns the things to which it applies. A more specific concept can have more defining attributes but fewer instances. Keep the meanings fixed when making that comparison; do not confuse the word's length with its logical role.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: An idea or concept is what we grasp mentally; a term is its expression in language. A term can contain several words, such as school library. In traditional terminology, intension or comprehension concerns the defining attributes of a concept, while extension concerns the things to which it applies. A more specific concept can have more defining attributes but fewer instances. Keep the meanings fixed when making that comparison; do not confuse the word's length with its logical role.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Library and school library can be compared in a Buea discussion. School library adds a qualifying attribute and applies to a narrower class of libraries. The expression contains several words but functions as one term. Counting letters would not tell us which objects fall within its extension.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Separate the expression, its meaning and the instances it covers. Give an example and a non-example when testing a proposed definition. Narrowing a concept is not the same as proving that a particular object exists. Teachers should confirm the course's preferred labels comprehension and extension.
